cf.title: Expose checkpoint timestamp and duration in pg_stat_checkpointer

input.subject: [PATCH] Expose checkpoint timestamp and duration in pg_stat_checkpointer

verdict_reasoning: The review stops at level 1b. The thread cites no monitoring tool or operator that asked for last-only gauges (demand-1). pg_control_checkpoint(), the num_* counters and the total= field of the log line already give the same data (already-exists-1). The "checkpoint starting:" line already prints the checkpoint flags (already-exists-2). The log change has support in message #2, so the goal may be fine once the author answers these points.

brief.title: Add last checkpoint duration and time to pg_stat_checkpointer, checkpoint type to logs
brief.problem: Monitoring tools that read pg_stat_checkpointer see only cumulative counters such as write_time and sync_time, so they cannot easily spot one slow checkpoint or unusually frequent checkpoints. The checkpoint complete log line also does not say which kind of checkpoint ran. The author hit this while debugging checkpointer write behavior.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds two gauges to pg_stat_checkpointer that each checkpoint overwrites: the duration of the most recent checkpoint and its end time. Separately, the checkpoint complete log line, emitted when log_checkpoints is on, names the checkpoint type, such as immediate, timed or manual. The author agreed to split these two changes into separate patches.
user_visible_surface: New column last_checkpoint_duration in pg_stat_checkpointer, in milliseconds; first named checkpoint_total_time.
New column last_checkpoint_time in pg_stat_checkpointer, a timestamp of the last checkpoint end.
New SQL functions behind the columns, such as pg_stat_get_checkpointer_checkpoint_total_time.
The checkpoint complete log message gains the checkpoint type in parentheses, for example "checkpoint complete (immediate)".
Fields added to the PgStat_CheckpointerStats struct in pgstat.h.
author_claims: A monitoring agent can alert when last_checkpoint_duration jumps, for example from about 300 ms to 5000 ms, even if several checkpoints ran between samples.
last_checkpoint_time lets tools detect checkpoints that run closer together than expected.
These signals are hard to get from cumulative write_time and sync_time without complex delta calculations.
The new columns complement the cumulative fields and replace nothing.
Many existing monitoring dashboards lack such checkpoint signals.
brief.thread_state: Michael Banck supports the log change but doubts the value of last-only gauges, because a poller misses checkpoints between samples and no other view stores a last duration. Álvaro Herrera does not want to block it but asked for a sleep-time breakdown; the author's May 2026 revive got no replies and the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: No full, split patch set has been posted; the last attachment looked incremental on the first.
The proposal does not say whether restartpoints on a standby update the new columns.
The proposal does not say how the duration separates active write and sync time from checkpoint_completion_target sleeps, which Álvaro asked for.
The proposal does not say how the log change names checkpoints triggered by WAL volume, or other reasons beyond manual, timed and immediate.
No documentation hunk is shown for the new columns or the changed log message.

prior_attempts.title: Add last_vacuum_index_scans in pg_stat_all_tables
prior_attempts.quote: No other stats counter works that way; they are all additive.
prior_attempts.reason: Alvaro Herrera objected that the column keeps only the last vacuum's value, unlike other stats counters, which are all additive; he and Peter Geoghegan said a history of vacuum runs would be more useful. Fujii Masao asked whether one global counter in a pg_stat_vacuum view would be enough, and Alvaro later doubted the tuning value because autovacuum memory is capped at 1 GB. The author did not resolve these points, and the visible thread ends with a request for a rebased patch that got no reply before the entry was withdrawn.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: Same pattern of a last-run-only value in a cumulative stats view, applied to checkpoint duration instead of vacuum index scans; the additive-stats objection is not answered.

prior_attempts.title: add the last checkpoint kind to the control file
prior_attempts.who_objected: Julien Rouhaud, Kyotaro Horiguchi, Michael Paquier
prior_attempts.quote: For now we have some room, but we will likely keep consuming bytes in that file for more critical features and it's almost certain that at one point we will regret wasting 2 bytes for that.
prior_attempts.reason: Reviewers saw no realistic use for the kind of an already completed checkpoint and preferred a pg_stat_progress_checkpoint view for the checkpoint in progress. The control file must stay within 512 bytes, so its space is kept for critical data, and two bytes for non-critical data were judged a likely future regret. The stored flags also leave out flags added when a running checkpoint is upgraded, for example by a later CHECKPOINT command. The author agreed to drop the patch.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: Reports the last checkpoint kind in the completion log line instead of the control file, so the control-file space concern does not apply; the upgraded-flags issue may still apply.

objections.title: No user demand shown for last-only checkpoint gauges
objections.failure_scenario: A monitoring vendor polls pg_stat_checkpointer every minute while checkpoints run every 20 seconds during a write spike. Its alert sees one duration out of three and misses the slow one. Everyone then keeps two new columns and functions that the target users cannot rely on.
objections.argument: The only use case offered is the author's own debugging session (message #1), plus a hypothetical agent in message #14. No field report, -general thread or monitoring tool asking for this is cited. Michael Banck stayed unconvinced (messages #2, #11, #13), Álvaro Herrera wanted a sleep-time breakdown first (message #3), and the May 2026 revive (message #15) got no reply. [P4] was withdrawn after a similar last-only column met the objection that stats counters are additive.
objections.author_must_show: Which monitoring tool or operator has asked for a last-checkpoint duration, and why do cumulative counters plus log_checkpoints not meet that need?

critic.reasoning: Álvaro calls the value useful in message #3, but the thread cites no field report or tool request, and the May 2026 revive got no reply. [P4] concerns design and must not be used as support for a demand objection.

objections.title: Per-checkpoint duration and time are already in logs and pg_control_checkpoint()
objections.failure_scenario: A monitoring tool reads last_checkpoint_time from pg_stat_checkpointer and checkpoint_time from pg_control_checkpoint(). The first is the checkpoint end and the second is its start, so they never match. Users find out when dashboards disagree, and they have two "last checkpoint" sources to keep apart.
objections.argument: pg_control_checkpoint() already returns the time of the latest checkpoint or restartpoint. The "checkpoint complete" line, logged by default under log_checkpoints, already gives total= per checkpoint, which pgbadger reads (message #7, #8). A poller can detect frequency from num_timed, num_requested and num_done. The author says this is "hard to get" without delta math (message #14), but that describes less convenient, not impossible.
objections.author_must_show: What can a tool do with the two new columns that it cannot do with pg_control_checkpoint(), the num_* counters and the log_checkpoints total= field?

critic.reasoning: pg_control_checkpoint() does return the last checkpoint time, and the complete line carries total= for every checkpoint. Message #14 says the existing route is harder, which does not show that it cannot do the job.

objections.title: Checkpoint type is already logged in the checkpoint starting line
objections.failure_scenario: With log_checkpoints on, each checkpoint already emits "checkpoint starting: immediate force wait" or "checkpoint starting: wal". The patch repeats a subset of those flags on the complete line. Log parsers that match the complete line must change, and the two lines can show different flag sets.
objections.argument: Michael Banck and the author both treat the type as missing from the log (message #2, #5), but the starting line lists the flags. Pairing a start line with the next complete line is a documented, modest step that pgbadger already performs. The proposal names only manual, timed and immediate, which is fewer than the starting line shows, such as wal and end-of-recovery.
objections.author_must_show: What does the type on the complete line give that the existing checkpoint starting line, which already lists the flags, does not?

critic.reasoning: The "checkpoint starting:" line does print the flags, and the thread never weighs it against the new text. The claim that pgbadger already pairs the two lines is not in the material and should not be used as support.

other_surviving.title: Last-only gauges repeat a design rejected for vacuum stats
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A monitoring agent polls pg_stat_checkpointer every minute while a WAL spike forces a checkpoint every 20 seconds. The agent sees only the last of three durations and misses a slow one in the middle. The operator finds out only when reading the server log, which already had all three.
other_surviving.argument: [P4] proposed a last-run-only column in a stats view and was withdrawn after the objection that cumulative stats are additive. Message #13 raises the same point here: no other view stores a last duration, and pollers miss checkpoints between samples. The reply in message #14 says checkpoint timing is special but does not answer the missed-sample case, and message #3 supports the column only as a stopgap. The May 2026 revive in message #15 got no response.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why is a last-only gauge better here than an additive form, such as a cumulative total duration or counters that a poller can turn into deltas?

critic.reasoning: Message #13 asks why only checkpoints get a last duration, and message #14 does not answer the missed-sample case. The point holds for the duration only, because last-event timestamps such as last_vacuum and last_archived_time already exist.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Changed checkpoint complete log line can break existing log parsers
other_surviving.failure_scenario: An operator upgrades to the release with this change while pgbadger or a site regex matches "checkpoint complete: wrote". The new "checkpoint complete (immediate): wrote" text no longer matches. Checkpoint charts and alerts go empty, and the operator finds out only after looking for missing data.
other_surviving.argument: Message #7 names pgbadger as the most widely used checkpoint report, and message #8 confirms it parses the server log. The proposal puts new text between the fixed prefix and the colon, which is the part parsers anchor on. The thread praises the log change (messages #2 and #11) but does not discuss what it does to existing parsers. Appending the kind as a trailing field would leave the prefix unchanged.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why put the type inside the message prefix instead of appending it as a new field that existing parsers would ignore?

critic.reasoning: Earlier changes to this line added fields after the colon and kept the "checkpoint complete:" prefix. The thread does not discuss parsers, and message #8 confirms pgbadger reads this log line.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: New checkpoint type words differ from the flags in the starting line
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A DBA matches the "checkpoint starting:" line with its "complete" line by kind. The start line prints existing flag words such as "time", "wal" or "immediate force wait". The complete line prints "manual", "timed" or "immediate" instead. The two names do not match, and a WAL-triggered checkpoint has no named type at all.
other_surviving.argument: The starting log line already reports the checkpoint flags, so a vocabulary for this exists. Message #1 introduces a second set (manual/timed/immediate) and does not say how WAL-volume, end-of-recovery, shutdown or combined flags are named. Message #2 asks about WAL-based checkpoints, which this list does not cover. [P5] records that a stored kind misses flags added when a running checkpoint is upgraded, and the same issue applies here.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Will the complete line reuse the exact flag words from the starting line, including wal and combined flags, and print them for restartpoints too?

precedents.title: add the last checkpoint kind to the control file

critic.reasoning: The starting line already prints flag words such as "time", "wal" and "immediate force wait". The proposal uses manual/timed/immediate and does not say how it names the WAL-triggered case that message #2 asks for.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Restartpoints on a standby are not addressed by the new gauges
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A monitoring agent polls last_checkpoint_duration on a hot standby, or on a primary just promoted from one. The value either never changes or shows restartpoint durations under a checkpoint name. The operator alerts on, or misses, a slow checkpoint that never happened on that node.
other_surviving.argument: The diff quoted in message #11 sets the gauges in LogCheckpointEnd(), which takes a restartpoint argument and runs on standbys too. pg_stat_checkpointer already counts restartpoints in separate columns, so callers expect the two to be kept apart. The proposal does not say whether a restartpoint overwrites last_checkpoint_* or what a newly promoted primary shows before its first checkpoint.
other_surviving.author_must_show: On a standby and right after promotion, what do last_checkpoint_duration and last_checkpoint_time show, and how does a tool tell a restartpoint from a checkpoint?

critic.reasoning: The diff quoted in message #11 sets the gauges in LogCheckpointEnd(), which also runs for restartpoints. The view counts restartpoints in separate columns, and the proposal does not say which events overwrite the gauges.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: A gauge in a summed stats struct needs its own flush and reset rules
other_surviving.failure_scenario: After pg_stat_reset_shared('checkpointer'), last_checkpoint_time goes back to empty even though the cluster has a recent checkpoint. Later work on checkpointer stats flushing treats every PgStat_CheckpointerStats field as a delta and sums it. A test that only checks counters going up does not catch the wrong value.
other_surviving.argument: The diff quoted in message #11 adds last_checkpoint_duration as a PgStat_Counter next to cumulative fields and assigns it, where the other fields are added. The proposal does not say how flush, snapshot and reset treat a field with set semantics, or whether restartpoints on a standby update it. With no comment or check, whoever next changes this code has to know the field is an exception.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How do reset, flush and restartpoints treat the two gauge fields, and what stops a later change to checkpointer stats from summing them by mistake?

critic.reasoning: Checkpointer stats flush by adding pending values and reset by subtracting an offset, so an assigned field needs its own handling in both paths. The proposal does not say how the gauges behave there.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Logged checkpoint type may not match how the checkpoint ran
refuted.failure_scenario: A timed checkpoint is running when an administrator issues CHECKPOINT, so the checkpointer finishes without throttling. The completion line still reports the original type. The DBA reads "timed" and attributes the unthrottled I/O spike to the schedule, not to the manual request.
refuted.argument: [P5] stored the kind of the last checkpoint, and its recorded review noted that the stored flags leave out flags added when a later request upgrades a running checkpoint. This proposal reports the type in the completion log line and lists only manual, timed and immediate. The thread does not say which flags it reports, or how it names WAL-triggered checkpoints and checkpoints that a later request upgraded. Message #2 wants exactly that WAL-based case.
refuted.author_must_show: Which flags does the log line report, and how are WAL-triggered checkpoints and checkpoints upgraded by a later request named?

precedents.title: add the last checkpoint kind to the control file

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which covers both the unnamed WAL-triggered case and the flags added when a later request upgrades a running checkpoint.

refuted.title: Last-only duration gauge departs from the cumulative stats view convention
refuted.failure_scenario: A monitoring tool polls every minute while checkpoints run every 20 seconds. It records only one of three durations and misses a slow one. After pg_stat_reset_shared('checkpointer') or on a standby running restartpoints, the tool cannot tell whether the gauge was cleared, kept or never set.
refuted.argument: Message #13 notes that no other view stores a last duration. [P4] was withdrawn after the objection that "No other stats counter works that way; they are all additive." The proposal does not say how reset and restartpoints affect the gauges, while existing last_* timestamps have defined reset behaviour. Message #14 explains why checkpoints are a special case, but it does not address the sampling gap that message #4 raised.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is a last-only gauge better than a cumulative total_time counter plus num checkpoints, and what do reset and restartpoints do to it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1 for the last-only convention and the sampling gap. Its reset and restartpoint questions are covered by maintenance-fit-2 and replication-ondisk-1.

refuted.title: Overwrite-only gauges do not fit the additive cumulative stats model
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator runs pg_stat_reset_shared('checkpointer') or restarts after a crash, which discards stats. The gauges then show zero or a stale value while the counters restart at zero. A tool that compares last_checkpoint_time with stats_reset or with counter deltas reports wrong checkpoint intervals.
refuted.argument: Fixed-numbered stats like pg_stat_checkpointer are built as counters that pending stats add to and that reset by offset. Message #13 notes that no other view keeps a last duration, and [P4] was withdrawn after the objection that all stats counters are additive. The proposal does not say how reset, crash discard, and pending-stats flush treat a value that is overwritten.
refuted.author_must_show: After a stats reset or crash recovery, what values do the two gauges show, and why is that correct for a monitoring tool?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-2, which asks the same question about reset, flush and snapshot handling of an overwritten field.

refuted.title: Last-only gauges set a new pattern in cumulative stats views
refuted.failure_scenario: After this lands, similar patches add last_vacuum_duration, last_analyze_duration and last_flush_duration to other pg_stat views on the same argument. Each one adds a column whose value is overwritten between polls. A tool polling every minute during a burst of 20-second checkpoints sees one of three durations and cannot tell that it missed the other two.
refuted.argument: Michael asked in message #13 why checkpoint duration needs a last-only value when no other view keeps one, and noted in message #4 that a poller misses checkpoints between samples. Message #14 answers that checkpoint timing is a special signal, but the same claim fits vacuum, analyze or WAL flush just as well. [P4] was withdrawn after the objection that no other stats counter works this way. Álvaro in message #3 chose not to block it but called a last-only value limited.
refuted.author_must_show: What rule separates checkpoint duration from vacuum or analyze duration, so later last-only gauges can be judged by it and not accepted one by one?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1. Both rest on message #13's question of why checkpoints alone get a last duration, on [P4], and on the same missed-sample scenario.

refuted.title: Changing the checkpoint complete line affects log parsers for little new data
refuted.failure_scenario: A site upgrades, and a log parser that matches the "checkpoint complete:" prefix stops counting checkpoints, or counts them as unknown. The DBA notices weeks later when the checkpoint report is empty. The flags were already in the "checkpoint starting:" line that the same setting emits.
refuted.argument: Messages #7 and #8 say pgbadger reads these log lines, so the format reaches external tools the project does not control. With log_checkpoints, the "checkpoint starting:" line already prints the flags, such as immediate, force, wal and time. The proposal names only manual, timed and immediate and does not say how combined flags or WAL-triggered checkpoints would appear. Each new checkpoint flag then needs a second label to keep up to date.
refuted.author_must_show: What does the complete line give that pairing it with the existing starting line does not, and how does it name combined or WAL-triggered checkpoints?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1 for the parser breakage and of already-exists-2 for the flags already printed on the starting line.

refuted.title: Existing counters and log_checkpoints already cover the stated alerts
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator who wants to alert on frequent checkpoints already computes the delta of num_timed and num_requested between polls. The new last_checkpoint_time adds a value that tells the operator less, because it does not count checkpoints between polls.
refuted.argument: Message #14 names two alerts: a sudden slow checkpoint and unusually frequent checkpoints. Counter deltas detect frequency, and the delta of write_time plus sync_time divided by the checkpoint count gives an average duration (message #4). log_checkpoints is on by default and records every checkpoint's total time, which pgbadger already charts (messages #7, #8). The author calls the delta approach complex, but monitoring tools already do it.
refuted.author_must_show: What concrete checkpoint problem would the new columns catch that counter deltas or the log_checkpoints lines miss?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1, which makes the same case from counter deltas and log_checkpoints and adds pg_control_checkpoint().

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The gauges are set where restartpoints also end, so standbys are affected and the proposal does not say how.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patch adds functions to pg_proc.dat and columns to pg_stat_checkpointer in system_views.sql.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds fields to the PgStat_CheckpointerStats struct in pgstat.h.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Overwritten fields sit in a struct of summed counters, and the changed log line reaches external log parsers.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: pg_control_checkpoint(), the num_* counters and the log_checkpoints lines already expose the last checkpoint time, duration and flags.

questions: Which monitoring tool or operator has asked for a last-checkpoint duration, and why do cumulative counters plus log_checkpoints not meet that need?
What can a tool do with the two new columns that it cannot do with pg_control_checkpoint(), the num_* counters and the log_checkpoints total= field?
What does the type on the complete line give that the existing "checkpoint starting:" line, which already lists the flags, does not?
Why is a last-only gauge better than an additive form, such as a cumulative total duration that a poller can turn into deltas?
On a standby, after promotion and after pg_stat_reset_shared('checkpointer'), what do last_checkpoint_duration and last_checkpoint_time show?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the cumulative statistics code and the checkpointer. Álvaro Herrera and Michael Banck commented early, but nobody replied to the May 2026 revive.
committability.liability: The owner signs for two columns with set semantics in a summed stats struct, their reset and restartpoint behaviour, and a log line format that external parsers read, for every later release.
committability.author_follow_up: The author agreed to split the patch, revived the thread in May 2026 and keeps moving the CommitFest entry forward, but no rebased, split patch set has been posted.

not_now.evidence_that_would_change_it: A request from a monitoring tool or operators for a last-checkpoint duration would change it. So would a concrete checkpoint problem that counter deltas, pg_control_checkpoint() and the log_checkpoints lines cannot detect.

priority.reason: The patch is about 7 KiB and touches xlog.c and the checkpointer stats code, but the gauges have no shown demand and need their own reset and flush rules. The log change has support and could go ahead alone once it is split out and reuses the flag words of the starting line.

provisional_note: No full, split patch set was available. Without the code, this review could not check how reset, flush and restartpoints treat the gauges, or which flags the complete line prints.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Report checkpoint progress with pg_stat_progress_checkpoint
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Michael Paquier, Andres Freund, Julien Rouhaud
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started as a proposal to log checkpoint progress in the server log. After objections it became a pg_stat_progress_checkpoint view that reports the checkpoint phase, flags, start LSN, start time and per-phase counters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The final close came because the author stopped responding after Andres Freund marked the patch waiting on author for a docs build failure and noted that the architectural feedback had not reached a conclusion. Earlier, Michael Paquier returned it because the view was too complex and carried fields of little use, such as next_flags, start LSN and most flag values. Julien Rouhaud objected that the view showed the initial checkpoint flags instead of how the checkpoint was behaving now. Andres Freund measured progress-update overhead in BufferSync() on large shared_buffers.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: There has been no updates on this thread for some time, so this has been switched as Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add checkpoint stats of snapshot and mapping files of pg_logical dir
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds statistics about logical decoding snapshot and rewrite mapping files in pg_logical to the checkpoint complete log message, such as count, time and cutoff LSN. After review it was cut down to one aggregate time, "logical decoding processing", plus a separate patch that deduplicates the checkpoint/restartpoint log messages.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Earlier objections about message length and translation were addressed. Nathan Bossart marked v12 ready for committer, and the author set it back to ready for committer after an unrelated pg_upgrade test failure on Windows. The entry was then withdrawn with no visible explanation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Report checkpoint progress with pg_stat_progress_checkpoint
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a pg_stat_progress_checkpoint view that reports the phase, flags, start LSN and other details of the running checkpoint or restartpoint. It started as a proposal to log checkpoint progress in the server log, but reviewers asked for a progress view instead.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with Feedback because the view needed simplification: several fields and flags were of little use for monitoring, and the phase names were too long. Andres Freund objected that the view definition makes pg_rewrite bigger, and he asked for proof that the progress counters do not slow down checkpoints with many dirty buffers. The last measurement shown, a manual checkpoint taking 2.457 s with the patch against 2.334 s without, got no reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think that what's proposed could be simplified, and we had better remove the fields that are not that useful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add last_vacuum_index_scans in pg_stat_all_tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a last_vacuum_index_scans column to pg_stat_all_tables that shows how many index scans the last vacuum of each table needed. The author meant it as a signal for raising maintenance_work_mem or autovacuum_work_mem.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Alvaro Herrera objected that the column keeps only the last vacuum's value, unlike other stats counters, which are all additive; he and Peter Geoghegan said a history of vacuum runs would be more useful. Fujii Masao asked whether one global counter in a pg_stat_vacuum view would be enough, and Alvaro later doubted the tuning value because autovacuum memory is capped at 1 GB. The author did not resolve these points, and the visible thread ends with a request for a rebased patch that got no reply before the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.objectors: Julien Rouhaud, Kyotaro Horiguchi, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: Store the flags of the last completed checkpoint (shutdown, end-of-recovery, immediate, force and so on) in the control file. Show them through pg_control_checkpoint() and pg_controldata, so users can see the checkpoint kind without reading the server logs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers saw no realistic use for the kind of an already completed checkpoint and preferred a pg_stat_progress_checkpoint view for the checkpoint in progress. The control file must stay within 512 bytes, so its space is kept for critical data, and two bytes for non-critical data were judged a likely future regret. The stored flags also leave out flags added when a running checkpoint is upgraded, for example by a later CHECKPOINT command. The author agreed to drop the patch.

For now we have some room, but we will likely keep consuming bytes in that file
for more critical features and it's almost certain that at one point we will

precedents_retrieved.title: Add last failed connection error message to pg_stat_wal_receiver
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stores the WAL receiver's last connection failure message in shared memory and shows it as a new last_conn_error column in pg_stat_wal_receiver and pg_stat_get_wal_receiver(). The goal is to let users see why replication connections fail without reading server logs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier said the patch covers only connection errors and misses other WAL receiver failures, such as an incorrect system ID or a TLI-related report; capturing FATAL errors would need shared memory. He also noted that the string is not reset when the WAL receiver starts, and that pg_stat_wal_receiver returns no rows when pid is NULL, so the column is only visible through the function. The author offered alternatives and said he was fine to withdraw if none was worth pursuing, and the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: Emit "checkpoint skipped because system is idle" message at LOG level if log_checkpoints is set
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Justin Pryzby, Kyotaro Horiguchi, Julien Rouhaud
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch raises the "checkpoint skipped because system is idle" message from DEBUG1 to LOG when log_checkpoints is set. The goal is to show in the server log that no checkpoints happened during idle periods.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Justin Pryzby argued that a message about doing nothing is a debug message, and that writing it can wake idle disks, for example through syslog fsync. He also noted that log_checkpoints became the default partly so that an idle instance would not write logs every 5 minutes. Kyotaro Horiguchi and Julien Rouhaud also voted -1 and suggested other ways to see skipped checkpoints, such as emit_log_hook or a counter in pg_stat_bgwriter. With no agreement, Justin Pryzby asked the author to close the CF entry, and it was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think it would be odd to write logs of increased severity, for the case where
we did not do anything.  I think it really is a debug log.

precedents_retrieved.title: Force the old transactions logs cleanup even if checkpoint is skipped
precedents_retrieved.summary: When a timed checkpoint is skipped because the system is idle, the patch still removes old WAL segments that have already been archived, after a KeepLogSeg() call that keeps segments needed by replication slots or wal_keep_size. The goal is for Postgres to free pg_wal on its own after a temporary archive_command failure, with no manual CHECKPOINT.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier did not think the case justified more code in the skipped-checkpoint path, and said it does not solve disk space issues reliably. Andres Freund agreed the scenario needs a fix but questioned this approach: a needed checkpoint may fail to write its WAL record when the disk is full, and freeing space should not have to wait for a checkpoint. He suggested that the archiver delete old WAL files after archiving them, and the visible messages show no revised patch along those lines.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If a checkpoint does have to
happen, we might not get to the point of removing the old segments, because we
might fail to emit the WAL record due to running out of space. And if that
doesn't happen - do we really want to wait till a checkpoint finishes to free
up space?

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server"
Reverted commit(s): Reduce checkpoints and WAL traffic on low activity database server Previously, we skipped a checkpoint if no WAL had been written since last checkpoint, though this does not appear in user documentation. As of now, we skip a checkpoint until we have written at least one enough WAL to switch the next WAL file. This greatly reduces the level of activity and number of WAL messages generated by a very low activity server. This is safe because the purpose of a checkpoint is to act as a starting place for a recovery, in case of crash. This patch maintains minimal WAL volume for replay in case of crash, thus maintaining very low crash recovery time.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 18fb9d8d21a28caddb72c7ffbdd7b96d52ff9724.  Per
discussion, it does not seem like a good idea to allow committed changes to
go un-checkpointed indefinitely, as could happen in a low-traffic server;
that makes us entirely reliant on the WAL stream with no redundancy that
might aid data recovery in case of disk failure.

This re-introduces the original problem of hot-standby setups generating a
small continuing stream of WAL traffic even when idle, but there are other
ways to address that without compromising crash recovery, so we'll revisit
that issue in a future release cycle.

roaster_notes.note: The pg_stat_progress_checkpoint attempts ([P1], [P3]) and the log-message attempts ([P2], [P7]) cover a different idea, and their recorded reasons do not apply here.
The log-line change has no persistent or cross-node state. The view change adds only shared-memory stats fields and a system view, which need a catversion bump and nothing in pg_upgrade.

The proposal has no real privilege or exposure aspect. pg_stat_checkpointer is already readable by all users and shows cluster-wide checkpoint counters and timings. A last duration and end timestamp add no new data about other users, sessions or query texts. The log change only adds the checkpoint type to a message that only privileged users can read.
Objections found. Committability: no committer has taken ownership. Álvaro and Michael commented in message #3 and message #11, and the May 2026 revive in message #15 got no reply.
Two objections raised; both concern existing ways to get the same data.
The checkpoint type in the log line has positive feedback (messages #2, #11), so this review raises no demand objection to that change.
